question.text: Indravati Growth Capital (Cat II) is planning to raise INR 500 crore across domestic HNIs, family offices and an offshore SWF anchor. The manager is evaluating Placement Agents and Distributors. Which statement BEST captures their role?

answer.text: Placement agents replace SEBI-registered merchant bankers for PPM filing
Placement agents are only required for offshore feeder structures

Placement agents and distributors are important for SELLING units AND for creating wider awareness/familiarity with AIF products among investors; a distributor can be empanelled with more than one AIF and can be individuals or institutions (distribution companies, broking firms, banks)
Placement agents are SEBI-registered trustees of the AIF

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, distributors and placement agents play a key role in selling AIF units and in creating wider awareness and familiarity with AIF products, services, investment strategies, and return potential. A distributor can be empanelled with more than one AIF, and can be either an individual or an institution such as a distribution company, broking firm, or bank. The Trap: The MB-replacement option confuses placement agents with merchant bankers (who handle PPM due diligence). The offshore-only option over-restricts the placement-agent role. The trustee option conflates two distinct service-provider categories. Note: Distribution and placement fees should be disclosed and paid in accordance with the workbook's disclosure-and-payment framework for AIF distribution fees.
